# Liandre John de Castro

> Tech Lead · Enterprise Digital Platforms. 6+ years building enterprise digital
> platforms for global pharmaceutical and consumer health brands, with end-to-end
> ownership of a Magnolia CMS platform behind 150+ localized websites. Based in
> Quezon City, Philippines. Primary audience for this site: technical recruiters.

## Summary

- Tech Lead at Crescendo Collective, leading 7 engineers across Java, Next.js, and Azure.
- Owns architecture and delivery of a reusable Magnolia CMS platform serving 150+ localized sites across 10 global brands, replacing one-off site builds with shared platform capabilities.
- Led technical solutioning and three client POC demos that secured a $1M statement of work.
- Architected an AWS serverless product data platform (Node.js, Lambda, API Gateway) that retired a legacy system and cut annual operating costs by 30%.
- Built a self-service "Website Kiosk" that cut site provisioning from days to minutes and saved 1,000+ engineering hours a year.
- Mentored 15 engineers; 5 now lead workstreams independently.
- B.S. Electrical Engineering, University of the Philippines Diliman (cum laude).

## Headline stack

- Java — backend systems, services, and integrations (Java 17, Spring, Spring Boot).
- Next.js — front-end and web application delivery (React, TypeScript).
- AWS — cloud architecture and serverless platforms (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB).
- Magnolia CMS — enterprise CMS platform work.
- Supporting: Node.js, SQL/PostgreSQL, Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions CI/CD.

## AI engineering

- Ships production work with AI-assisted development (Claude Code, ChatGPT).
- Prompt and context engineering: designing prompts, context, and workflows for reliable LLM results.
- Applies AI in real engineering work to accelerate delivery, raise code quality, and support technical decisions across a team. A force multiplier on the stack above, not a replacement for it.

## Blog

- [How I Built a CRO Copywriting Workflow in Claude Code](https://liandrejohn.com/blog/how-i-built-a-cro-copywriting-workflow-in-claude-code) — how a fixed pipeline of Claude Code skills, subagents, and reference material replaces one long correction-heavy chat: an orchestrating skill, four narrow subagents (researcher, strategist, copywriter, critic), a selectively-loaded references folder, and a written evaluation rubric — walked through with a fictional nighttime-supplement landing page so no real client work is exposed.
- [How I Built My Portfolio with Claude Code](https://liandrejohn.com/blog/how-i-built-my-portfolio-with-claude-code) — how this site itself was built with Claude Code: the useful part wasn't asking AI to write more code, it was giving it a smaller, clearer system to reason inside, then reviewing each decision before it shipped. Covers prompt and context engineering with scoped CLAUDE.md instruction files, the Vite/Bootstrap stack, structured data for AI answer engines, and a from-scratch AWS deployment pipeline.
- [How I Deployed My Portfolio to AWS Without Overengineering It](https://liandrejohn.com/blog/how-i-deployed-my-portfolio-to-aws) — the smallest production-ready AWS stack for a static site: Amazon S3 for storage, CloudFront as the CDN, Route 53 for DNS, ACM for HTTPS, and GitHub Actions for deployment, with IAM OIDC so no long-lived AWS keys sit in GitHub. Also covers clean URL canonicalization (dropping .html, forcing the apex domain) with a single CloudFront viewer-request function. No servers, no containers, no Terraform.
- [How I Actually Built It — Next.js, MongoDB, and an AI Coding Agent](https://liandrejohn.com/blog/how-i-built-unboxed) — the technical build story behind Unboxed: a deliberately boring stack (Next.js App Router, Bootstrap + Sass, MongoDB + Mongoose, Web3Forms, Google Places, AWS Amplify), the six-step spec-first workflow (document, branch, implement, verify, commit, log) followed for every feature, and the verification habits — a real database script checking real rejected inputs — that made it a codebase worth trusting. Part 2 of 2; Part 1 covers why the project exists.
- [I Own 8 Board Games. Here's What I Built Around Them.](https://liandrejohn.com/blog/why-i-built-unboxed) — the story behind Unboxed, a board-game rental side project for Metro Manila run solo: GCash payment and Lalamove delivery checked by hand, explicit policies (payment before confirmation, deposit-vs-rental-fee refunds, cancellation terms, a multi-game discount), and a site that's responsible for exactly three things — availability, pricing, and the Metro Manila delivery boundary. Part 1 of 2; [Part 2](https://liandrejohn.com/blog/how-i-built-unboxed) covers the technical build.
